name: ROYAL READING
clue: Commissioned at the 1604 Hampton Court Conference, this English translation of scripture appeared 7 years later

name: A PLACE IN THE NAME
clue: Born in 1820 while her wealthy English parents were touring Italy, the founder of modern nursing was named for her birth city

name: DOUBLE-0 ONCE
clue: This Australian played James Bond exactly once, in 1969's 'On Her Majesty's Secret Service'

name: GREAT EXPECTATIONS
clue: Born a minor German princess named Sophie, she seized the Russian throne from her own husband in a 1762 coup

name: SHAKESPEARE'S ROMANS
clue: Banished by the city he had saved, this general marches an enemy army to Rome's gates in the Shakespeare tragedy named for him

name: THE PERIODIC TABLE
clue: Element 98, first created in 1950 at a university cyclotron, takes its name from the state where it was made

name: BARRIER TO ENTRY
clue: Manhattan's famed finance lane takes its name from a wooden palisade the Dutch erected in the 1650s to guard New Amsterdam

name: SCANDALOUS PREMIERES
clue: Fistfights broke out at the 1913 Paris premiere of this Stravinsky ballet about a pagan sacrifice

name: SEVEN WONDERS
clue: Of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, it's the only one still largely standing today

name: ONCE IN A LIFETIME
clue: Mark Twain was born 2 weeks after its 1835 appearance and died, as he had predicted, the day after its 1910 return

name: RUN FOR THE AGES
clue: This barefoot Ethiopian palace guard won the 1960 Olympic marathon on Rome's cobblestones, then won again in Tokyo wearing shoes.

name: CROSS PURPOSES
clue: Honoring founder Henry Dunant's homeland, the Red Cross flag reverses the colors of this country's square banner

name: HIGH & DRY
clue: Astronomers prize the cloudless skies over this Chilean desert, the driest non-polar place on Earth and home to the ALMA observatory.

name: AT THE OPERA
clue: Puccini died before finishing this opera; at its premiere, Toscanini laid down his baton where the composer had stopped

name: INITIAL HERE
clue: A congressman's error on his West Point paperwork gave this Ohio-born Union commander & future president the apt initials 'U.S.'

name: LOGO LEGENDS
clue: The dribbling silhouette in the NBA's logo was modeled on this Lakers guard nicknamed 'Mr. Clutch'

name: DOUBLE LAUREATES
clue: This American chemist is the only person to win two unshared Nobel Prizes: Chemistry in 1954 and Peace in 1962

name: BACK FROM THE DEAD
clue: Revived from liturgical use into an everyday spoken tongue, this ancient language became official in the new state of Israel in 1948.

name: ANCIENT GAME NIGHT
clue: Called weiqi in China and baduk in Korea, this territorial board game defied computers until AlphaGo's landmark 2016 victory.

name: HOME COURT ADVANTAGE
clue: The Flushing Meadows home of tennis's US Open is named for this champion, who won 1973's 'Battle of the Sexes'

name: DEMOTION COMMOTION
clue: An 11-year-old English schoolgirl named this world discovered in 1930; its 2-letter symbol also honors Percival Lowell

name: FAB FOUR SOLO
clue: Though credited to the Beatles, this 1965 ballad features only Paul McCartney and a string quartet

name: POSTHUMOUS POETS
clue: Fewer than a dozen of her poems appeared in print before her death in Amherst in 1886; nearly 1,800 surfaced afterward

name: SWAN SONGS
clue: Dead at 35 in 1791, this Salzburg-born prodigy left his Requiem unfinished; his pupil Süssmayr completed the mass

name: LONG LIVE THE KING
clue: Becoming king at age four, this French monarch reigned 72 years, outliving both his son and his grandson

name: RING RECORDS
clue: In 1956 this heavyweight champion retired with a perfect 49-0 record, a mark no heavyweight titleholder has matched

name: PEN NAMES
clue: Author Eric Blair took his famous pen surname from an English river he loved to walk beside

name: ACCIDENTAL PRESIDENTS
clue: He's the only person to serve as both U.S. vice president and president without being elected to either office

name: MIDDLE OF NOWHERE
clue: Nicknamed for a Jules Verne captain, this oceanic 'pole of inaccessibility' is where space agencies aim their retiring spacecraft.

name: GODS ON THE CALENDAR
clue: English names this weekday for the Norse thunder god; the French 'jeudi' honors Jupiter, Rome's own thunderer
